issue.title: Agent-hood publication requests in the research hood stall at attempts=0 and never drain, so the outbox WARN never clears
issue.description:
DISCOVERED BY: sase-oc.land while committing the epic's landing integration work. NOT caused by epic sase-oc (shell completion) — the requests predate the commit by 31-42 hours and are in the 'research' hood, which the epic never touched.

OBSERVED (2026-08-17, workspace sase_12, athena):
'sase doctor --json' check state.agent_publication_outbox reports WARN. Project gh_sase-org__sase holds 20 requests: 0 quarantined, 0 retired, 3 stalled. The three stalled entries are

  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cdx      age 41.6h  attempts=0  last_error=null
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cld      age 41.5h  attempts=0  last_error=null
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.final_3  age 31.3h  attempts=0  last_error=null

each with reasons ['stalled: age >= 1d 0h']. The other two projects (actstat, bob-cli) hold zero requests. state.agent_publication_digest is OK with 0 problems, so this is not digest drift.

THE DEFECT: attempts=0 with last_error=null means the drain path has never once attempted these requests. Because they are never attempted they can never fail, so they can never accumulate attempts, retire, or quarantine either — they are invisible to every existing remediation. 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' does not touch them (it clears quarantined requests, and these are not quarantined); 'sase agent sync --drop-retired' does not either (they are not retired). They simply age indefinitely and hold state.agent_publication_outbox at WARN for every agent that runs 'sase doctor' on this host.

Contrast with the working path: during the same session a real quarantine (19 requests, 'file digest mismatch') was reported by sase_git_commit and 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' cleared it completely — quarantined_request_count went 19 -> 0 and the digest check went to OK. So the quarantine machinery works; it is specifically the never-attempted requests that have no path out.

SCOPE: find why the full-sync drain skips these three requests (a hood-selection or publishability filter that silently excludes them is the likely shape, given attempts stays 0), then either make the drain attempt them — so they succeed, or fail into the existing retry/quarantine/retire lifecycle — or give them a deliberate terminal state. A request the drain refuses to attempt should not be able to sit at attempts=0 forever with no recorded reason.

REPRODUCTION: sase doctor --json, then read checks[] entry state.agent_publication_outbox -> data.problems. Note the check identity lives on the 'id' field; 'name' is absent, so a probe matching on 'name' silently finds nothing.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-fi — closed task 'Prompt-archive publication has no durable retry path'. Its description states that agent-hood publication already HAS a durable retry via the agent-publication outbox, which is exactly the mechanism failing here: the outbox holds these requests but never attempts them. Its fix is working — this session's commit printed 'prompt archive publication was deferred and will retry with agent publication', the retry-with-agent-publication path sase-fi added.

RELATED: sase-hw — closed task 'sase commit quarantined-publication warning recommends a retry that can never clear v2 import identity collisions'. Distinct root cause: in this session the recommended 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' DID clear all 19 quarantined requests, so the warning's advice was correct here. The stalled attempts=0 requests are a separate class that no advice covers.

RELATED: sase-fk — closed task 'Repair bob-cli agents sidecar digest drift and clear its publication outbox residue'. Same subsystem and a similar symptom, but that task was a one-time bob-cli repair and both bob-cli's outbox and the digest check are clean now; this is a live sase-project stall with no digest component.

evidence.note:
INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION + ROOT-CAUSE DIAGNOSTIC (sase-op.land, workspace sase_13, athena, 2026-08-17T21:0xZ, master d5ac42693).

Answers this bead's SCOPE question directly. The three stalled requests are NOT skipped by a hood-selection or publishability filter. They are attempted and they FAIL, on hood-level relationship validation:

  could not publish agent hood 'research': invalid hood relationships: duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'

HOW OBSERVED: 'sase_git_commit' (sase stitch create, create_commit) for the epic sase-op land diff pushed the commit successfully and then printed: 'Primary commit succeeded; agent-hood publication is queued and will retry automatically. Last error: <the message above>'. That commit's drain pass is what finally attempted these requests.

STATE AFTER, from 'sase doctor --json' -> checks[state.agent_publication_outbox].data.problems — same three global_agents this bead names, now with a recorded attempt:

  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cdx      age 41.9h  attempts=1  last_error=<above>  primary_revision d5f2d8fe86c7fd0aeb4743aabc0ad9ebbb78e72a
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cld      age 41.9h  attempts=1  last_error=<above>  primary_revision e35d3831e1adc005a5cb65c071e947080b1b9693
  bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.final_3  age 31.7h  attempts=1  last_error=<above>  primary_revision 9b2560f8689ecf28ccfb0223bc0358418e0974aa

All three still quarantined=false, retired=false, terminal_reason=null, reasons=['stalled: age >= 1d 0h'], remediation_command still the inapplicable 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined'. Project sase outbox moved 20 -> 12 requests (quarantined 0, retired 0, stalled still 3); actstat and bob-cli remain empty.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX: the attempts=0/last_error=null state this bead was filed on was a not-yet-attempted state, not a permanently-skipped one — a drain does reach them. The durable defect is narrower and now concrete: every attempt fails identically because agent hood 'research' has invalid relationships (a duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'), and attempts=1 with a populated last_error still does not advance toward retire or quarantine, so they remain invisible to both documented remediations and hold state.agent_publication_outbox at WARN. Two things to fix: (1) repair or reject the duplicate 'research.h.final' container relationship so the hood can publish, and (2) let a deterministically-failing request escalate into the retry/quarantine/retire lifecycle instead of restalling at the same age reason with a remediation command that cannot apply to it.

NOT CAUSED BY epic sase-op (glossary command); that epic touches src/sase/glossary/**, the Justfile symvision line, and docs only, and these requests predate its land diff by 31-42 hours.

evidence.note:
INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION + ROOT CAUSE, 2026-08-18 ~19:30 EDT, workspace sase_14, athena. Discovered by sase-q3.land during sase_git_commit, which warned that the sase project holds quarantined agent-hood publication requests. NOT caused by epic sase-q3 (gate input panel); no in-progress epic has a causal link.

THE THREE REQUESTS THIS BEAD NAMES NOW HAVE A REAL last_error. research.0m.cdx, research.0m.cld, and research.0m.final_3 are no longer at attempts=0/last_error=null. 'sase agent sync --check --json' now reports them under quarantine_diagnostics as:

  publication request bbugyi200.athena.research.0m.cdx@d5f2d8fe86c7 quarantined after 3 attempts: could not publish agent hood 'research': invalid hood relationships: duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'; run 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' to retry

So half of this bead's requested remediation has already happened on its own: the drain DOES now attempt them, and they DO fail into the existing retry/quarantine lifecycle. What remains is that they still never drain, and now we know why.

ROOT CAUSE: the 'research' hood has a corrupt relationship graph — a duplicate or inconsistent container global name 'bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final'. This is a hard data-integrity failure, not a transient one, so 'sase agent sync --retry-quarantined' can never clear these; they will re-exhaust their 3 attempts and re-quarantine on every retry. That is why the outbox WARN never clears. The fix is to repair or de-duplicate the research hood's container relationships (or give a hood that fails relationship validation a deliberate terminal/retired state) rather than to make the drain retry harder.

BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD RECORDED. The sase project now holds 52 quarantined requests, in four groups:
  - 12 x 'invalid hood relationships: duplicate or inconsistent container global name bbugyi200.athena.research.h.final' — every research.0m/0o/0p/0q/0r request (cdx, cld, final/final_2/final_3). This bead's defect; permanent, unretryable.
  - ~34 x 'agents sync lock is busy' after 3 attempts — transient contention; genuinely retryable, but the 3-attempt budget is exhausted by lock contention alone on a busy multi-workspace host.
  - 1+ x 'agent-hood publication did not complete within 120s' after 3 attempts — timeout; retryable.
  - 4 x 'file digest mismatch', all on 'agents/bbugyi200.athena.<id>--mon/chat.md' — digest drift confined to monitor-hood chat transcripts, i.e. a --mon hood's chat.md keeps changing after its snapshot is signed. 'sase agent sync --repair-digests' (added by sase-fa.4, used by closed sase-fk for bob-cli) is the existing tool for this half.

IMPACT: state.agent_publication_outbox stays WARN for every agent on this host, and sase_git_commit prints a quarantine warning on every commit telling the agent to run a retry that cannot succeed for the research group.

REPRODUCTION: timeout 180 sase agent sync --check --json, then read projects[] where project == 'sase' -> quarantine_diagnostics (52 entries; group them by the text after 'attempts: ').
